title: Doppelgängers: Hey you, you're me!
summary: Josh and Chuck explore doppelgangers, starting with a tour-date reminder and Francois Brunel's photo series "I'm Not a Look Alike!" pairing strangers who resemble each other. They trace the word "doppelganger" to Jean Paul's 1796 novel Siebenkäs, cover folklore (seeing your double three times means death, the Norse vardøger), literary doubles (Poe's William Wilson, Dostoevsky's The Double, Living with Yourself), and historical accounts (Lincoln, Percy Shelley, Catherine the Great, Goethe). They discuss a study of 32 doppelganger pairs showing genetic similarity but no relation, a Tegan Lucas facial measurement study estimating one-in-a-trillion odds, and the Neil Douglas Ryanair seat encounter. The brain's face-recognition region (fusiform gyrus) and the bias of facial recognition AI are covered, followed by real-life body doubles and political decoys (Kim Jong Un, Saddam Hussein, Stalin, Montgomery's double Clifton James). The episode ends with a listener email from Elkie about Ashkenazi Jewish matchmaking and genetic screening, a follow-up to the Kissing Cousins episode.

segments.title: Tour reminder and intro to doppelgangers
segments.summary: Josh gives a Pacific Northwest tour reminder, then introduces the day-after-Labor-Day episode on doppelgangers and Francois Brunel's photo series of strangers who look alike.
topics: I'm Not a Look Alike photo series

segments.title: Origin of the word doppelganger
segments.summary: The word is German, meaning double goer or double walker, coined by Jean Paul in his novel Siebenkäs at the end of the eighteenth century, who misspelled the term he meant to use.

segments.title: Doppelganger folklore and superstitions
segments.summary: Discussion of folklore: seeing your doppelganger three times means death in England and Germany, and the Norse vardøger arrives before you on journeys.

segments.title: Literary doubles
segments.summary: Hosts cover doubles in literature: Poe's William Wilson, Dostoevsky's The Double, and the Paul Rudd series Living with Yourself, plus TV uses like Three's Company.

segments.title: Historical doppelganger accounts
segments.summary: Accounts of historical figures who reportedly encountered doppelgangers, including Lincoln, Percy Shelley, Catherine the Great, and Goethe, with the hosts debating which count as true doppelgangers.

segments.title: Genetics of doppelgangers
segments.summary: Discussion of Brunel's photo project and a study by Manel Estellor on 32 doppelganger pairs: AI facial recognition matched half as identical twins, and genomes showed shared SNPs but no relation, with epigenetics and microbiomes random.

segments.title: Facial measurement odds and how we recognize faces
segments.summary: Tegan Lucas's study of four thousand faces from an Army database estimates a one-in-a-trillion chance of matching across eight features; the hosts discuss odds across the global population, and how people use shortcuts to recognize faces.

segments.title: Face swaps, fusiform gyrus, and facial recognition bias
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Bush-Cheney face swap meme, how people register faces, the fusiform gyrus face-recognition region, and bias in facial recognition AI that led to wrongful arrest of Niger Parks.

segments.title: Celebrity doubles and political decoys
segments.summary: Career options for doppelgangers such as photo doubling and stand-ins, and political decoys including Kim Jong Un, Saddam Hussein, Stalin, and Clifton James impersonating Bernard Montgomery before D-Day.

segments.title: Ryanair seat and doppelganger encounters
segments.summary: Neil Douglas found his doppelganger sitting in his seat on a Ryanair flight to Ireland, and Sean McCartel met his double floating in a Las Vegas pool; the hosts estimate tens of thousands of similar-looking people.

segments.title: Listener mail: Ashkenazi matchmaking and genetic testing
segments.summary: Elkie writes about insular Ashkenazi Jewish community practices of recessive gene screening and matchmaking, responding to the Kissing Cousins episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and sign off.
